label: Homicide rate
reliability_criteria: Canonical tier = WHO Mortality Database cause-of-death registrations as submitted by member states (civil registration, ICD-coded, Assault = X85-Y09 and predecessors), redistributed by the OECD Causes of Mortality dataflow over SDMX, 49 countries, 1960-2024, sex-split as published; witness tier = UNODC intentional-homicide compilation via OWID (criminal-justice and vital-registration sources with imputation, near-global, 1990-2023). Authenticity first per ADR-0008: the two tiers count differently and are displayed beside each other, never blended.
license: Mixed, per source (see "sources"): OECD DF_COM = OECD Terms and Conditions, attribution required (content: WHO Mortality Database); OWID witness = CC-BY-4.0.
notes:
THE THIRD PILOT GOES TWO-TIER (P3): until v7 this indicator was the review's standing gap — mono-OWID, no canonical/witness treatment. The canonical is now the WHO Mortality Database route: national civil-registration deaths by cause, as submitted, ICD-coded, carried by the OECD "Causes of mortality" (DF_COM) dataflow over its public SDMX API. Content judgment: the registrations are as-reported (not modeled) — the same collector-tier judgment as UN DYB, and the contrast with GHO's own homicide indicators (literally named "Estimates of ...", harmonized) marks the line.
THE SEX SPLIT IS TODD-RELEVANT SIGNAL: the dataflow publishes per sex, and the as-reported numbers are stark — Russia's assault mortality 1994 crisis peak: male 52.5 vs female 14.3 per 100k (3.7x). The (entity, year, sex) merge key carries it end-to-end, exactly like life_expectancy.
THE CRUDE-RATE PIN (anti-derivation discipline): the dataflow also carries age-standardized rates for the same keys (RUS 1994 male: crude 52.5 vs standardized 63.3 per 100k) — standardization adjusts for age structure, a derived comparability measure, NOT the as-reported rate. The canonical tier fetches CALC_METHODOLOGY=CRUDE only; the age-standardized variant is a witness-tier concept and is deliberately absent.
HONEST SCOPE LIMITS (collector holes are data, see the-measurement-problem.md): 49 countries (OECD + key partners incl. Russia, China, Brazil, South Africa, India, Colombia) — NOT near-global; most of Africa and Central Asia absent, Ukraine and Belarus absent from this dataflow. Russia's series ends 2019 (the WHO MDB's own lag): 2020+ is witness-only there — a divergence to display, not a gap to patch.
WITNESS TIER: owid `homicide-rate-unodc` — the UNODC compilation (criminal-justice + vital-registration sources, with imputation for missing country-years), near-global 1990-2023. Vital-registration assault (canonical) vs criminal-justice homicide (witness) differ where deaths are classified differently than they are investigated: the comparison IS the point.
reclassification_sensitive=true: the homicide/suicide/accident/ "undetermined intent" boundary shifts with the quality of a country's cause-of-death certification system — relevant to the reclassification test mentioned in the brief ("ill-defined" categories).
